diagnosis: Customer upgraded to business plan mid-cycle on the 14th and received an invoice higher than the list price, likely due to prorated charges as described in kb-0001. To provide a line-by-line explanation, the specific disputed line item and expected amount would be needed per kb-0009, but the general proration logic should address the immediate concern.
reply:
When you upgrade mid billing cycle, the first invoice includes a prorated credit for the unused portion of your old plan and a prorated charge for the new plan for the remainder of the cycle. This means the total can differ from the listed plan price. This is a one-time adjustment—subsequent invoices will reflect the standard Business plan rate.

If a specific line on invoice INV-88213 still doesn’t make sense, let us know which line and the amount you expected, and we’ll take a closer look.
